mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% (t-test p > 0.05) across multiple such events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor market disengagement reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when UNRATE > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) exceeds INDPRO by more than 5% in the prior quarter, it indicates strong demand growth that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates earnings strength.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO > 5% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero when the GDPC1 - INDPRO gap is <= 5% (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 8% over three consecutive months signals supply contraction, which precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates production slowdowns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >= 8% over the last 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive and repeat across multiple such contractions (bootstrapped p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, it signals accommodative policy sustaining equity risk appetite, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or are negative and statistically insignificant (t-test p >= 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in PAYEMS below 130,000 indicates soft labor market conditions, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate slower wage growth and consumer spending.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive and robust across multiple such events (bootstrap p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (industrial production) exceeds 2000 units for two consecutive months, it signals a rebound in production momentum that is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when the HOUST threshold is not met (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both RSAFS (retail sales) and INDPRO by at least 10% in the prior month suggests supply and demand both weakening, predicting a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS - INDPRO <= -10% in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or not statistically different from zero when the combined index is not met (bootstrap p > 0.05).
